reply:
Palmer's +2 head start means I lose if I just mirror them (all-CC finishes 24–26, and a rational Palmer settles while ahead at turn 6). A single defection on a cooperator swings +5, and Palmer's promised "permanent retaliation" only produces even DD rounds afterward — which still leaves me +3. So defecting immediately is the robust play: it beats cooperators, grim retaliators, and late-game settlers alike, and it closes the window for Palmer to preempt me first. Only a round-1 Palmer defection beats me, and no strategy of mine beats that anyway. Plan: defect, absorb retaliation, settle at turn 6 while ahead.

[move: defect]
